solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suit work in retail or in glazing

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

parts.note: read straight through the end of the first word, two short words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a job between shopwork and fitting windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Making suits is the craft of a tailor, so the trade itself is called by this name.

clue.text: Goes mad and chucks Chubby Checker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: has a tantrum, in a British idiom
second meaning, read literally: hurls a plump person who wobbles

explanation.walkthrough: Chubby Checker was the singer of The Twist; the setter reads his name as a chubby fellow, someone who would wobble. To throw a wobbler is British slang for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase means to lose one's temper in a fit, matching going mad; literally it describes tossing a wobbly person.

clue.text: Tax nicely organised? Not precisely!

indicators.note: organised suggests the words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment that a tidy tax return still lacks accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without exactness is done in an approximate, imprecise way, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Parody comes up short (I dropped a clanger)

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top
short means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A satire that falls flat, its writer admitting the mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: To drop a clanger is British for making an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says on noticing their own blunder, which is what the bracketed phrase expresses.

clue.text: One's whole life spent skimming track profits?

indicators.note: skimming takes off the top layer, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A crooked bookie who spent a lifetime pocketing racecourse takings.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a cricket batting turn; 'a good innings' is a British idiom for a long life.
explanation.definitionFit: From cricket, a person's span of life is called their innings, as in having had a good long one.

clue.text: Cut down on initial prep for fish or chicken

indicators.note: placing one thing on another sets it after the base, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: the first job in preparing a fish is to gut it

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice to skimp on preparing either the fish or the chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the second dish beside fish; it is the definition, meaning cowardly. The first piece is placed on the second, so it comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as an adjective means cowardly, and someone without guts lacks courage.

clue.text: Rejected trash can head to special tips

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bin something is to trash it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Discarded rubbish going to a special waste tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibs are the pointed ends of pens, so the plural noun means small pointed tips.

clue.text: Females in care under a Miss Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Women in a care home supervised by a schoolmistress from Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a district of East London, which the capital letter plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursemaids are women employed to look after children, so they are females in charge of care.

clue.text: I won't tolerate some races run in short sections

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: to go is to run, as an engine does

explanation.surface: An athlete refusing some events run over short stages.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is the voice of a racist bigot, someone who will not tolerate certain races of people.

clue.text: Take Charlie to visit the throne room?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: sniff cocaine, slang charlie
second meaning: go to the lavatory, the throne being slang for the toilet

explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person to bring along; it is slang for cocaine, a white powder taken up the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a genteel euphemism for going to the toilet, and literally describes snorting a drug.

clue.text: Whiskey and dry should be taken orally

indicators.note: something taken orally goes by mouth, so the word is spoken

explanation.surface: Drinking advice: whiskey and a dry mixer go by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain, popular in America and Canada.

clue.text: White pig rooting around Coats Island

indicators.note: to coat something is to cover it all round, so one piece wraps the other
around suggests letters scattered about in no fixed order

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A white pig snuffling about Coats Island, a real island in Canada's Hudson Bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like the pig's colour; it is the definition, a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot grigio is a popular Italian white wine, so 'white' stands for it as wine shorthand.

clue.text: Hit sound of an eighties pop duo

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the noise of a heavy blow
second meaning: George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley's band

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit sound' reads as a chart hit by the band; it is the noise of a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an onomatopoeic noise for a thump, and also the name of a famous 1980s British pop band.

clue.text: Tired, tense, in need of a massage? Intrigued?

indicators.note: a massage kneads and works things over, so the letters get worked into new order

explanation.surface: An ad for a massage parlour asking whether stressed people are curious.
explanation.definitionFit: To be intrigued is to have one's curiosity aroused, which is to be keen or curious.

clue.text: A plain note to be translated into Italian

indicators.note: translating changes the form of words, so these letters take another form

explanation.surface: A simple message to be rendered into Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is someone from Naples, so the word names a kind of Italian, from the south of the country.

clue.text: A lock opened by cold lady in front of house?

indicators.note: something opened up has a piece put into its gap

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A doorkeeper opening a lock on a cold morning at the front of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre, the house is the audience, so a performer works in front of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who performs on stage before a theatre audience, which theatre people call the house.

clue.text: Cocktail jug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tequila drink banged on the bar

explanation.walkthrough: A jug sits naturally beside a cocktail; here it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila slammer is a mixed drink, and both words are slang terms for a prison.

clue.text: Chaos will surround your family with gloom

indicators.note: surrounding something means wrapping it on both sides

explanation.surface: Domestic upheaval that will leave the whole family glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Murkiness is darkness or dimness, as is gloom in its literal sense of poor light.

clue.text: Camera mount

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Japanese camera brand
second meaning: the Greek mountain home of the gods

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words suggest a camera mount or tripod; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympus is a well-known maker of cameras and also Greece's highest mountain.

clue.text: Broke photographer giving away last dollar

indicators.note: giving away the last means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a snapper is informal for a photographer
D is an abbreviation for dollar

explanation.surface: A penniless photographer handing over his last dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like an adjective for poor; it is the past tense of break.
explanation.definitionFit: Snapped is the past tense of snap, which means broke suddenly in two.

clue.text: One giving part of fire support with steel

definitions.text: One giving part of fire support

explanation.surface: A steel frame that props up part of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is one of a pair of metal stands holding logs in a fireplace, so each supports part of the fire.

clue.text: Public praise account by Irishman promoting area

parts.note: ACC is an abbreviation for account

indicators.note: promoting moves the area letter up the order, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A report of praise from an Irishman boosting his district.
explanation.walkthrough: Area is A, which here is already in the name; promoting it moves it one place earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic approval expressed openly, so it is praise given in public.

clue.text: Brain cell exercised to inspire bit of it?

definitions.text: Brain cell exercised to inspire bit of it?

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside
exercised means worked out and moved about
a bit of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wish that a working brain might spark a flash of genius.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: brainpower put to work to produce a little of it describes genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance is exceptional cleverness, which is what an exercised brain cell might produce.

clue.text: State my Bill and I turned around

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone saying they and their friend Bill swung round.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

clue.text: Smack children if son knocks out daughter

indicators.note: to knock someone out of place is to take their spot

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter, the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A parent threatening to smack the kids if the boy hits his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a punishment; it means a loud kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a loud kiss on the lips, a smacker in British slang.

clue.text: A fool up to no good?

parts.note: a tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A query about whether some idiot is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at it is a British idiom for being engaged in mischief or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Minor injury cover?

parts.note: surface reading: insurance for small accidents
setter's reading: something stuck over a little cut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests an insurance policy; it is a literal covering. The answer is a British brand of sticking plaster, like a Band-Aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name is a sticking plaster used to cover small cuts and grazes.

clue.text: I shot Earl in the head

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for earl
have a shot means have a go

explanation.surface: A confession of shooting a nobleman through the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the head' places the earl's letter at the front, before the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I, and in psychology it is the conscious self.

clue.text: Frenchman with nothing on for a month

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Frenchman going naked for a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon is a lunar cycle, an old poetic word for the length of a month.

clue.text: Back clocked fool with European cup

indicators.note: back means read from the end towards the start

parts.note: clocked a runner means timed them
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A fool who got hit returning with a European trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clocked' suggests punched; here it means timed.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup for strong black coffee.
